subject: biology
examFormat: Biology is one of the three sections in the single combined EJU Science (理科) booklet; examinees choose 2 of the 3 subjects and answer on a mark-sheet (one subject per side). The 2 chosen subjects share an 80-minute limit. The biology section comes last in the booklet (roughly pages 39-56) and consists of a flat list of about 16-18 independent numbered questions (問1-問18 in recent papers; answer rows 1-18). Like chemistry there are no Roman-numeral super-blocks; questions progress roughly in topic order from cell biology/molecular biology, through genetics and development, body regulation (homeostasis, nervous/endocrine/immune systems, sensory organs, muscle), plant physiology, ecology, evolution and phylogeny. Some items split into sub-parts (1) and (2) sharing one figure. Every item is single-best-answer multiple choice (choose ONE, typically from 4-8 options). Common answer formats: choose the correct/incorrect statement; choose the combination from a table (assign a/b/c or A/B/C to terms); order events into a sequence; read a graph or diagram (survivorship curve, oxygen-dissociation curve, antibody-titer curve, energy-flow table, population-growth graphs) and select the right interpretation; and a few short genetics calculations (recombination frequency, segregation ratio, required number of mother cells). Text is Japanese with extensive bilingual glossing of biological terms (English in parentheses). No calculator; the few calculations use simple arithmetic. There is essentially no chemistry-style numeric heavy lifting - biology is concept-, diagram-, and reasoning-driven.
taxonomyNote: No EJU 2026 Biology syllabus PDF is present in the Drive folder. This taxonomy is derived from the official EJU Biology scope (which follows 'Basic Biology' and 'Advanced Biology' of the Japanese high-school Course of Study) combined with the biology topics actually observed in the 2018_2, 2019_1, 2020_2, and 2021_1 science papers.

questionArchetypes.description: Cell-structure presence/absence table or organelle statement: a table marks +/- for structures across prokaryote / animal / plant cells and you choose the combination assigning A,B,C to organelles (e.g. chloroplast, cell wall, mitochondria); or choose the correct/incorrect statement about an organelle (ribosome, chloroplast).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: A table shows +/- for structures in animal/plant/prokaryotic cells; assign A,B,C among chloroplast, cell wall, mitochondria. (2021_1 Q2; 3-column variant 2019_1 Q2; ribosome statement 2020_2 Q1; common prokaryote/eukaryote feature 2018_2 Q1)

questionArchetypes.description: Protein/ATP structure: label parts of a molecule (ATP: phosphate/ribose/adenine/adenosine), or choose true/false statements about protein structure levels (primary sequence, alpha helix/beta sheet as secondary, denaturation, number of amino acids = 20).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Given a schematic of ATP, choose the combination naming parts A-E (ribose, adenosine, phosphate, adenine, ADP). (2021_1 Q1; protein-structure statement set 2020_2 Q2 and 2018_2 Q2)

questionArchetypes.description: Respiration / electron transport: identify substances or compartments in a mitochondrion diagram (matrix/inner membrane/ATP synthase, NADH source), or order/assign the stages glycolysis/citric-acid-cycle/electron-transport and their inputs/outputs (O2, CO2, pyruvate).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Using a mitochondrion diagram, fill blanks a-c about the electron transport chain (protein complexes, matrix side, inner membrane). (2020_2 Q3; respiration-stage labeling A-D 2019_1 Q3)

questionArchetypes.description: Photosynthesis: assign reactions (CO2 reduction, water splitting/O2 release, light absorption) to photosystem I / photosystem II / Calvin-Benson cycle; or true/false on special photosynthesis (green sulfur bacteria, cyanobacteria carbon assimilation).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Assign reactions a (CO2 reduction), b (water electron donation, O2 release), c (light absorption) across photosystem I, photosystem II, Calvin-Benson cycle. (2021_1 Q3; green-sulfur-bacteria statement 2020_2 Q4; cyanobacteria assimilation 2019_1 Q1)

questionArchetypes.description: Nitrogen metabolism: identify the set of organisms that perform nitrogen fixation, or fill blanks about nitrogen assimilation vs nitrogen fixation and the role of root nodule bacteria and the products (protein, nucleic acid).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Choose the correct set of nitrogen-fixing organisms (e.g. Nostoc, Clostridium, Azotobacter, root nodule bacteria). (2021_1 Q4; assimilation/fixation blank-fill 2019_1 Q4)

questionArchetypes.description: DNA replication / transcription mechanism: choose the correct replication direction diagram, or fill blanks naming enzymes and 5'->3' direction (helicase, polymerase); or transcription/splicing blanks (RNA polymerase + promoter; mRNA precursor, introns removed, exons joined).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Fill a-c about DNA replication: helicase breaks hydrogen bonds, polymerase copies templates, new strand grows 5'->3'. (2020_2 Q5; replication-direction diagram 2019_1 Q5; transcription promoter/RNA-polymerase 2018_2 Q6; splicing exon/intron 2020_2 Q6 and 2021_1 Q5)

questionArchetypes.description: Genetic code from data: deduce a codon for an amino acid from synthetic-mRNA repeat experiments or from a codon table (point mutation case), choosing the original codon among options.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: From repeated synthetic mRNAs (UGUGUG..., UUGUUG..., GGUGGU...) and the resulting polypeptides, deduce the codon for cysteine. (2019_1 Q6; sickle-cell original codon from table 2020_2 Q7)

questionArchetypes.description: Genetic engineering / PCR: label A,B,C in an insulin-production scheme (human insulin gene, plasmid, E. coli), or fill PCR-principle blanks (hydrogen bond, primer, DNA polymerase).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: In an insulin gene-transfer scheme, identify A,B,C (plasmid, human insulin gene, E. coli). (2019_1 Q7; PCR-principle blanks 2021_1 Q6)

questionArchetypes.description: Meiosis / linkage genetics calculation: from a testcross segregation ratio compute recombination frequency, or determine new gamete genotypes and the timing of crossing over; or order meiosis-stage figures and give chromosome numbers; or which figures are haploid n.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: From a testcross [AB]:[Ab]:[aB]:[ab]=1:8:8:1, find the percentage of recombinant gametes. (2019_1 Q8; new-gamete-genotypes + crossing-over timing 2021_1 Q7; self-cross segregation ratio with linkage 2018_2 Q8; order meiosis figures + chromosome count 2018_2 Q7; haploid figures 2019_1 Q9)

questionArchetypes.description: Plant reproduction / development diagram: identify which cells fuse to form the embryo (double fertilization), which structures form the embryo sac, the number of embryo-sac mother cells for N seeds, where meiosis occurs; or label gastrula germ layers and cavities.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: In a mature pollen + embryo sac diagram, identify which two structures give rise to the embryo. (2020_2 Q9; double-fertilization statement 2018_2 Q9; meiosis location + mother-cell count 2021_1 Q9; gastrula A-C labeling 2021_1 Q8)

questionArchetypes.description: Circulatory/blood diagram interpretation: from a circulatory-system or heart diagram pick the vessel with least urea, most glucose after a meal, or most oxygen; identify venous-blood vessels, sinoatrial-node location, chamber names; or read an oxygen-dissociation curve to get oxyhemoglobin percentages at given O2/CO2 conditions.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: From a circulatory-system diagram, choose vessels with (I) least nitrogenous waste, (II) most glucose after eating, (III) most oxygen. (2021_1 Q10; heart vessels/chambers/SA node 2020_2 Q10; vessel X/Y oxygen/glucose 2018_2 Q10; oxygen-dissociation-curve percentages 2020_2 Q11)

questionArchetypes.description: Kidney filtration table: from concentrations of components in primitive urine vs urine, identify which is glucose / Na+ / protein based on filtration and reabsorption behavior.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Given primitive-urine and urine concentrations of three components, identify which is Na+, glucose, protein. (2019_1 Q11)

questionArchetypes.description: Blood-sugar / endocrine regulation: label autonomic nerves (sympathetic/parasympathetic) and hormones (insulin/glucagon/adrenaline) in a blood-glucose control diagram; or choose what happens on body-temperature drop (false statement).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: In a blood-glucose regulation diagram, name autonomic nerves I-III and hormones X-Z (insulin, glucagon, adrenaline). (2018_2 Q11; thermoregulation false-statement 2020_2 Q12; autonomic-nervous-system true-pair 2021_1 Q11)

questionArchetypes.description: Immunity: interpret an antibody-titer graph for primary vs secondary response (choose the curve), or choose the correct statement about immunity (secondary response, vaccine, HIV infects helper T cells, serotherapy).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Choose the graph showing antibody amount after 1st vs 2nd infection (secondary response is faster/larger). (2019_1 Q13; immunity correct-statement 2020_2 Q13)

questionArchetypes.description: Neuron / brain / sensory: choose the action-potential-vs-stimulus-strength graph (all-or-none), identify the brain region for movement/balance (cerebellum) or a reflex center, label retina cells (rod/cone) and light direction, or order cochlea pitch reception and identify fluids; muscle: order the contraction steps (Ca2+ -> troponin -> tropomyosin -> actin-myosin) or choose a correct muscle statement.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: As stimulus strength increases on one neuron, choose how action-potential size changes (all-or-none). (2020_2 Q14; cerebellum balance center 2019_1 Q12; retina rod/cone + light direction 2018_2 Q12; cochlea pitch order + fluids 2021_1 Q12; muscle-contraction step order 2021_1 Q13; muscle statement 2018_2 Q13)

questionArchetypes.description: Plant hormones / tropism / photoperiod / behavior: fill blanks on germination (gibberellin promotes, abscisic acid inhibits, amylase); interpret coleoptile phototropism experiments (mica/gelatin inserts) to deduce auxin movement; read an auxin-concentration vs elongation table/graph; determine flowering under light/dark regimes for a long-day plant; or identify a learning (vs innate) behavior example.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Fill blanks: in germination the embryo secretes [gibberellin], which promotes amylase; the inhibitor is [abscisic acid]. (2021_1 Q14; coleoptile mica/gelatin phototropism 2019_1 Q15; auxin concentration-response table 2018_2 Q14; long-day-plant flowering regimes 2020_2 Q17; learning-behavior example 2019_1 Q14)

questionArchetypes.description: Survivorship curve / population interaction: from survivorship-curve types choose which organism (and which curve) shows high early mortality; or interpret Paramecium single vs mixed culture graphs for niche similarity and coexistence (competitive exclusion).
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Among survivorship-curve types A/B/C, choose which organism shows high early then low later mortality and which curve it is. (2021_1 Q15; Paramecium competition niche/coexistence 2019_1 Q16)

questionArchetypes.description: Ecosystem energy budget: from a trophic-level energy table compute net primary production and a missing growth value; or fill blanks defining gross production, respiration, net production; or assign solar light -> chemical -> heat energy in the energy-flow statement.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: From a trophic-level energy table (feeding, death, respiration, growth) with gross production given, find net primary production and the missing value a. (2021_1 Q16; gross/net production definitions 2018_2 Q15; energy-form flow light/chemical/heat 2019_1 Q17)

questionArchetypes.description: Evolution mechanisms / phylogeny: fill blanks distinguishing genetic drift, natural selection, and mutation; order chemical-evolution steps; order major events in the history of life (plant/vertebrate land transition, dinosaur extinction, mammal radiation); or use a plant phylogeny tree, assigning traits (vascular bundle, ovule enclosed in ovary, seed formation) to branch points A/B/C.
questionArchetypes.exampleStem: Fill blanks a-c: genetic drift, natural selection, and mutation in how evolution proceeds. (2019_1 Q18; chemical-evolution order 2020_2 Q18; history-of-life ordering 2018_2 Q16; plant-phylogeny trait assignment 2021_1 Q17)

styleNotes: Generate about 16-18 independent single-best-answer items (問1-問18) in roughly this topic order: cell biology & biomolecules (incl. ATP/protein), metabolism (respiration, photosynthesis, nitrogen), molecular genetics (DNA replication, transcription/splicing/translation, genetic code, PCR/engineering), genetics & reproduction (meiosis, linkage/recombination calculations, plant & animal development), homeostasis (circulation/blood/oxygen-dissociation, kidney, endocrine/blood-sugar, autonomic/thermoregulation, immunity), nervous/sensory/muscle, plant physiology & behavior (hormones, tropism, photoperiod, learning), ecology (survivorship, populations, ecosystem energy), and evolution/phylogeny. Strongly favor authentic EJU biology formats: 'choose the correct/incorrect statement', combination-table items where you assign A/B/C or a/b/c to terms, ordering a process into a sequence, and figure/graph interpretation (cell-structure +/- tables, mitochondrion/chloroplast diagrams, circulatory-system and heart diagrams, oxygen-dissociation curves, antibody-titer curves, survivorship curves, energy-flow tables, coleoptile-experiment setups, plant phylogeny trees). Include a small number (1-3 per exam) of light genetics calculations (recombination frequency, segregation ratio, number of mother cells, energy-budget arithmetic) with clean numbers. Biology is concept- and diagram-driven, NOT calculation-heavy - keep numeric items rare and simple. Write stems in Japanese and gloss every biological term bilingually (Japanese with English in parentheses), exactly as the real exam does; describe figures in words since they are integral. One idea per item; difficulty matches Japanese high-school 'Advanced Biology' (standard university-entrance level).
